charts.title: Net Investment Result
charts.annotation: Only captured in the KPI table from FY2024; per the DCF build notes this line ranged from -HK$7.5bn (FY2022) to +HK$14.6bn (FY2025) over the full history.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

grossPremiums.title: Gross premiums written
grossPremiums.content:
Gross premiums written is the total insurance premium income underwritten before reinsurance ceded or reserving -- the core top-line KPI for a life/P&C insurer, parallel to "revenue" for an industrial company.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: this column is only populated FY2017-FY2021. From FY2022 the group reports under IFRS 17, which replaces gross premiums written with the "insurance revenue" / insurance service result presentation -- the series is not missing data, it is a regime change, and should not be compared across the break.

What to watch:

  • Growth in the pre-IFRS 17 years as a read on underwriting volume, not profitability
  • Use InsuranceServiceResult (profit chart) for the post-2022 equivalent of "how is underwriting doing"

netInvestmentResult.title: Net investment result
netInvestmentResult.content:
Net investment result is the insurer's income from its investment portfolio (interest, dividends, realised and unrealised gains/losses on the assets backing policyholder liabilities) net of related expenses.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: this is the single biggest swing driver of reported earnings -- per the DCF analyst's build notes it ranged from -HK$7.5bn in FY2022 (a market downturn year) to +HK$14.6bn in FY2025, though only the FY2024-FY2025 values are currently captured in the KPI table and charted here. FY2025's reported net income of HK$27.1bn is considered abnormal largely because of this line, not because underwriting or expense performance stepped up by a similar magnitude.

What to watch:

  • Whether a strong NetIncome year is backed by investment gains or by InsuranceServiceResult -- they are very different in persistence
  • Mark-to-market volatility from equity and bond holdings under prevailing accounting rules (IFRS 9/17)
  • Do not extrapolate a single year of net investment result into a DCF base case

repoLiabilities.title: Repo liabilities
repoLiabilities.content:
Repo liabilities are short-term borrowings secured by repurchase agreements over the insurer's bond/investment portfolio -- a funding and liquidity-management tool, not policyholder-related debt.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: repo liabilities reached HK$106.7bn in FY2025, a material funding line the DCF analysis flagged separately from TotalDebt -- it sits alongside insurance contract liabilities on the balance sheet and is generally excluded from the group's operating net-debt bridge, but its scale matters for liquidity risk.

What to watch:

  • Repo balance growth relative to the investment portfolio it is secured against
  • Refinancing/rollover risk in a rising-rate environment
  • Do not conflate with TotalDebt -- the two are tracked and used separately in the valuation

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China Taiping Insurance Holdings Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
